record.paper_title: Open questions for strongly interacting Fermi gases with zero-range interactions
record.original_question: In the high-temperature cluster expansion of a homogeneous two-component Fermi gas at unitarity, can one prove the conjectured general formula for every mixed sector (n↑,n↓) ≠ (1,1), expressing the cluster coefficient b_{n↑,n↓} as a mass prefactor times an integral over the logarithmic derivative of the Efimov function Λ_{n↑,n↓}(iS), plus the quantum-statistical correction from indistinguishable non-monoatomic subclusters? The formula is established for N = 3 and numerically supported in a special N = 4 equal-mass case, but a general proof requires control of the analytic properties of Λ_{n↑,n↓} in the complex plane.

evidence.quote: How to calculate the cluster coefficients bn↑,n↓? At the unitary limit a−1 = 0, the simplest way is to use the harmonic regulator method of reference [43], which first places the system in the harmonic traps Uσ(r) of Equation (2) and then, all calculations done, opens the traps to obtain the homogeneous case from the local density approximation (exact in the limit ω → 0+).
As a result, the cluster coefficients must be functionals of the Λn↑,n↓ of Equation (21). This is indeed what is predicted by the conjecture in reference [44]
The proof of expression (33) in the general case therefore remains open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a homogeneous two-component (spin ↑, spin ↓) Fermi gas in three dimensions with zero-range s-wave interactions tuned to the unitary limit (inverse scattering length a^{-1}=0). At high temperature, the grand-canonical pressure admits a virial/cluster expansion in the fugacities z_↑, z_↓ of the form

  P/(k_B T) = λ_T^{-3} Σ_{n_↑,n_↓ ≥ 0, (n_↑,n_↓)≠(0,0)} b_{n_↑,n_↓} z_↑^{n_↑} z_↓^{n_↓},

where λ_T is the thermal de Broglie wavelength and b_{n_↑,n_↓} are the (mixed) cluster coefficients. For each sector (n_↑,n_↓) with N = n_↑+n_↓ ≥ 2, let Λ_{n_↑,n_↓}(s) denote the Efimov-type spectral function defined as the regularized product (or appropriate analytic determinant) over the eigenvalues of the scale-invariant N-body unitary problem in a harmonic trap, viewed as an entire/meromorphic function of the complex variable s.

Conjecture to prove: For every mixed sector (n_↑,n_↓) with (n_↑,n_↓) ≠ (1,1) (and N ≥ 2), the unitary cluster coefficient is given by

  b_{n_↑,n_↓} = C_{n_↑,n_↓} ∫_0^∞ S · (d/dS) log Λ_{n_↑,n_↓}(iS) dS  +  Δ_{n_↑,n_↓},

where C_{n_↑,n_↓} is an explicit prefactor depending only on the masses and particle numbers, and Δ_{n_↑,n_↓} is the explicit quantum-statistical correction accounting for indistinguishable non-monoatomic subclusters (built from lower-order cluster coefficients in the standard Ursell/Mayer way).

The formula is known to hold for N = 3 (proved) and is numerically supported in a particular equal-mass N = 4 case. Establish the formula for all (n_↑,n_↓) ≠ (1,1); a complete proof requires control of the analytic properties (zeros, poles, growth) of Λ_{n_↑,n_↓}(s) in the complex plane.

status_evidence.title: Clustering of Four-Component Unitary Fermions
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical results on cluster coefficients of unitary fermions in the four-body sector, consistent with the Efimov-function conjecture but not a general proof.
status_evidence.claim: Only specific N≤4 cases have been verified, supporting that the general conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: The Four-Boson First-Excited State Near Two-Body Unitarity
status_evidence.snippet: Recent few-body work near unitarity continues to study Efimov-like spectra without proving the general cluster-coefficient formula.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature treats related few-body Efimov spectra; no general proof of the conjectured cluster-coefficient formula appears.
